sents.t: The day after Thanksgiving is called Black Friday.
It’s the day when holiday shopping begins, and stores offer huge sales.
Carlos, who loves a good deal, wanted a new TV.
“The store that has the best price opens at five in the morning,” he said.
“If we get there early, we’ll get one.”
At four thirty, it was freezing, and there were already two hundred people in line.
A man who had brought a camping chair told us he had been there since midnight.
When the doors opened, people ran in as if it were a race.
Carlos found the TV that he wanted, but there were only three left.
He grabbed one just before another man did.
“Sorry!” Carlos said, and the man laughed.
On Saturday, I worked at the bookstore.
It was Small Business Saturday, a day when people are encouraged to shop at stores that are owned by their neighbors.
We had more customers than ever, and many of them were people who had heard our podcast.
Tina, who has worked here for six years, said it was the busiest day she could remember.
That evening, I counted the money.
We had sold more books than on any other day this year.
Mr. Lee called to say thank you, and I went to bed at eight.
